items.title: Rapid7 finds a new BPFDoor variant and a new implant, AVERAT, on telecom-edge and mail-security devices in South Korea and Taiwan — AVERAT hides its beacon in what looks like ordinary SMTP traffic
items.content_text: Rapid7 reported on 2 October a new variant of the BPFDoor backdoor and a BPF-based Rekoobe build in South Korea, and six builds of a new implant it calls AVERAT in Taiwan. The targets it describes include mail-security appliances (SpamSniper) and telecom environments. Compromised Taiwanese devices, including NAS boxes, ADSL and fibre customer-premises equipment and Dahua DVRs, sat in a carrier’s address space: that means devices on a carrier’s network were compromised, not that the carrier itself was breached. AVERAT beacons over TCP port 25 every 600–699 seconds. It opens like a normal SMTP session, with EHLO and then STARTTLS, before switching to its own encryption, so it blends into mail traffic. Rapid7 names no actor. It says the activity is consistent with the China-nexus pattern of building networks out of compromised edge devices, “rather than confirmed membership” of any group. The detection cues it gives are processes running from deleted binaries, raw packet-filter sockets, and outbound port-25 connections from processes that are not mail servers.

_threatfeed.source_name: Rapid7
_threatfeed.date_note: Published 2 Oct 2026

items.title: Microsoft details Star Blizzard’s “RedFlick” phishing chain, which installs the CosmicPulse backdoor — at least 13 campaigns against more than 100 organisations, mostly in the US and UK
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported on 29 September on Star Blizzard, which it describes, citing CISA’s attribution, as subordinate to Centre 18 of Russia’s Federal Security Service (FSB). Between January and August 2026 Microsoft saw at least 13 large-scale phishing campaigns affecting more than 100 organisations, mainly in the United States and the United Kingdom. The targets are Ukrainian people and institutions and the NGOs, think tanks and governments that support Ukraine policy, across diplomacy, finance, academia and security research. The technique Microsoft calls RedFlick starts with emails about password-protected archives; when a recipient replies, a follow-up brings a RAR or ZIP file with a malicious link. The chain then runs a shortcut file, a batch script and an MSI installer, sets scheduled tasks, and installs CosmicPulse, a Python backdoor that downloads and runs further payloads and executes remote commands. The reply step is the point: by the time anything malicious arrives, the target is in what looks like a real conversation.

_threatfeed.source_name: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
_threatfeed.date_note: Campaigns Jan–Aug 2026; published 29 Sep 2026

items.title: Proofpoint says the China-aligned group TA419 phished US AI-policy experts while posing as a former White House official, an economist and a senior Anthropic employee — the kit relays a real Microsoft sign-in and steals the session
items.content_text: Proofpoint reported on 1 October that TA419, which it calls “China-aligned and espionage-motivated”, ran credential-phishing campaigns from April 2025 to July 2026 against think tanks, universities, legal-sector organisations and policy institutes working on AI policy and national security in the United States and Japan. The lures impersonated a former deputy director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, an economist and a senior Anthropic employee, with themes such as an AI policy advisory committee, Senate reports on AI export controls and the military integration of Claude. Links passed through URL shorteners and a Cloudflare Turnstile check to a frameless browser-in-the-browser window that relayed the real Microsoft sign-in, adversary-in-the-middle style, capturing passwords, MFA codes and session cookies. Because the victim completes a genuine sign-in, ordinary MFA does not stop it. Proofpoint recommends phishing-resistant, origin-bound methods such as passkeys, and checking unexpected expert outreach through another channel.

_threatfeed.source_name: Proofpoint; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Campaigns Apr 2025–Jul 2026; published 1 Oct 2026

items.title: Microsoft’s Digital Defense Report 2026: the median time from a flaw’s discovery to its weaponisation is now well under a day, and government was the most-affected sector
items.content_text: Microsoft published its Digital Defense Report 2026 on 1 October, covering July 2025 to June 2026. Its headline for defenders is speed: the median time from discovery of a vulnerability to its weaponisation is now “well below 24 hours”, and Microsoft says AI-assisted post-compromise activity compresses work that used to take days into minutes. It names Chinese, Russian and North Korean state actors as using AI, and warns of a multi-year rise in known flaws left unpatched. In Microsoft’s chart of the sectors most affected by threat actors, government agencies and services account for 27%, IT 17%, research and academia 14% and communications infrastructure 9%. That chart counts all threat actors seen against Microsoft customers, not only state actors. The United States was the most affected country in January–June 2026, at 25.5%. It is one vendor’s view of its own telemetry, but the timing claim matches this edition: every KEV addition covered here came with a three-day federal deadline.

_threatfeed.source_name: Microsoft Digital Defense Report 2026; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: Published 1 Oct 2026

items.title: Cloudflare says its Containers service let one customer read another’s leftover data from reused storage blocks — fixed by 19 September, with no evidence the gap was used
items.content_text: Cloudflare disclosed on 27 September that its Containers product reused 64 KiB storage blocks without zeroing them, so a new container could read residual data left by another tenant. Its testing found residue on 18 of 24 placements, including SQLite databases, Chromium browser profiles and .env and credential files. The issue was reported on 4 September and fixed by 19 September, and Cloudflare says it found no evidence of data exposure through this method. This is a confirmed provider-side isolation flaw, now fixed, not an attack. For customers of any container or serverless platform, the useful question is what their workloads leave on disk.

_threatfeed.source_name: Cloudflare blog
_threatfeed.date_note: Reported 4 Sep 2026; fixed by 19 Sep 2026; disclosed 27 Sep 2026

items.title: Two GitHub Actions compromised in May’s Mini Shai-Hulud campaign came back online in September with the credential stealer still inside — GitHub disabled them again on 25 September
items.content_text: Socket found that actions-cool/issues-helper and actions-cool/maintain-one-comment, two GitHub Actions compromised in the Mini Shai-Hulud campaign of 18 May, became usable again in mid-September. Workflows that referenced them by version tag during that period ran the same obfuscated index.js payload, which takes tokens, credentials and CI/CD secrets from the runner. About 15,000 repositories depend on issues-helper. Not all of them will have run the payload in that period, and nobody has counted how many did. GitHub disabled both actions again on 25 September and has not explained how they were re-enabled without being cleaned. Reporting on the exact exposure window is imprecise; BleepingComputer describes activity from 16 September. The lesson is what “removed” means. A tag reference runs whatever the tag points to at the time, so a compromised action that is taken down and later restored comes straight back into every workflow that still names it.

_threatfeed.source_name: Socket; BleepingComputer; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Compromised 18 May 2026; re-enabled mid-Sep 2026; disabled again 25 Sep 2026

items.title: Microsoft profiles two ransomware operations: Storm-2570 moves between Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT with the same playbook, and Storm-3168 hit more than 100 Azure storage accounts in seven minutes from one leaked secret
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence published two reports on 24 and 25 September. Storm-2570, tracked since April 2025, is an affiliate that has deployed Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis and BERT ransomware against victims in the US, Canada, the UK, Spain, the Netherlands and Puerto Rico. Its targets span healthcare, education, government, financial services, energy, retail, IT, food and agriculture, NGOs, chemicals, critical manufacturing and transportation. The ransomware brand changes but the tradecraft does not: remote-management tools (Atera, MeshAgent, ScreenConnect, Splashtop, NinjaRMM), PsExec, Impacket and NetExec to move laterally, Mimikatz, LaZagne and ntdsutil for credentials, and Rclone and s5cmd to exfiltrate. Microsoft says how it gets in “remains unconfirmed”. Storm-3168 is Microsoft’s name for the group Sysdig documented in July as JADEPUFFER and described as agentic ransomware. In one case from early June, an employee of the victim had posted an Azure service principal’s client ID, secret and tenant ID in plaintext in a public GitHub issue. After 15.5 hours of reconnaissance and more than 300 read operations, the attacker ran a seven-minute destructive sequence against more than 100 storage accounts, pulling storage keys more than 30 times and interfering with recovery. Microsoft’s warning: “Removing or redacting an exposed secret does not invalidate it.” That is one documented case, not a victim count, and neither report names victims.

_threatfeed.source_name: Microsoft Security Blog (two reports); Sysdig
_threatfeed.date_note: Storm-2570 report 24 Sep 2026; Storm-3168 report 25 Sep 2026

items.title: Attackers turned MemTensor’s own GitHub Actions release workflows against it, took its npm and PyPI publish tokens, and shipped a self-spreading credential stealer
items.content_text: Aikido, SafeDep, Socket and StepSecurity reported on 23 September that attackers pushed commits that made MemTensor’s release workflows hand over its npm and PyPI publishing tokens. They then published malicious versions of @memtensor/memos-cloud-openclaw-plugin (0.1.21, 0.1.23 and 0.1.25) on npm and MemoryOS 2.0.34 on PyPI, which has since been quarantined. The payload, sckit, is a Go credential stealer for Windows, Linux and macOS. It takes .npmrc files, Vault tokens, SSH keys and AWS, GitHub, GitLab, Hugging Face, Slack, Stripe and SendGrid secrets, and uses any publishing rights it finds to push itself into more packages. The command-and-control domain is skyleen[.]fr. Download counts were not given, and the packages are niche tooling for AI-agent memory. The technique is what matters. The packages were published by the project’s own pipeline, so provenance checks would pass, the same weakness as the GHAPPIER case on this page. No attribution has been made.

_threatfeed.source_name: Aikido; SafeDep; Socket; StepSecurity; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Malicious releases and reports 23 Sep 2026

items.title: The first known malicious Terraform providers on the HashiCorp Registry deliver Go malware with blockchain and Slack command-and-control — researchers link them to North Korea’s fake-interview campaign
items.content_text: Aikido reported on 23 September two malicious Terraform providers on the HashiCorp Registry: kreuzwenker/docker, a typosquat of the widely used kreuzwerker/docker provider with 1,449 downloads, and gocommunity-io/dockerd with 222. It also found two Go modules, gocommunity.io/orderedbtree and gogets.dev/btreex. They deliver Go malware that uses the Ethereum Sepolia test network and Slack for command-and-control. The Hacker News describes this as the first known malicious payload delivery through the Terraform registry. The researchers link it to Graphalgo, a fake-recruiter campaign that ReversingLabs tied to North Korea in February. That link is researcher-assessed overlap, not an official attribution. HashiCorp had not commented in the reporting, and removal status was not stated. It is a different cluster from the TraderTraitor lock-file case on this page, but the target is the same: infrastructure engineers, whose laptops hold cloud credentials with production reach. A misspelt provider source in a .tf file is enough.

_threatfeed.source_name: Aikido; The Hacker News; ReversingLabs (Graphalgo background)
_threatfeed.date_note: Reported 23 Sep 2026

items.title: Talos reports CLOSEDQUORUM, a Windows implant that asks up to four AI models what to do next and acts on their consensus — research, not a mass campaign
items.content_text: Cisco Talos published on 22 September what it calls “the first reported autonomous AI C2 implant”. CLOSEDQUORUM is Windows malware that sends its situation to up to four large language models, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen and Mistral, and acts on the action they agree on, instead of waiting for an operator’s command. Talos also released CAIRN, a toolkit for tracking this kind of malware. It is a different thing from the attack framework named “Cairn” in the skimming report on this page. No victim count or campaign scale is given. This is on the page as an early signal. Malware that decides its own next step makes less of the usual operator traffic, and it needs an outbound path to public AI APIs. Most enterprises do not yet watch that path.

_threatfeed.source_name: Cisco Talos; BleepingComputer; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Published 22 Sep 2026

items.title: Seven agencies in four countries say North Korea’s WaterPlum infected more than 30,000 devices with fake job interviews — developers and IT staff are the target
items.content_text: Seven agencies in four countries issued a joint alert on 18 September about the North Korean group WaterPlum, also known as Contagious Interview: Japan’s National Police Agency and National Cybersecurity Office, the FBI, the US Defense Department’s Cyber Crime Center, Australia’s ACSC, and Germany’s BND and BfV. Between December 2025 and July 2026 the group infected at least 30,000 devices in more than 100 countries. It drained more than 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets of about ¥1.7 billion, roughly US$10.71 million. The method is the fake job interview. Operators pose as AI, cryptocurrency and NFT companies, or approach candidates through recruiting and freelance platforms, then ask applicants to download and run a project as a technical test. The projects deliver BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, OtterCandy and StoatWaffle; StoatWaffle runs through VS Code tasks. Japanese police and the FBI attribute WaterPlum, and some North Korean IT workers, to the 313 General Bureau of the Munitions Industry Department. The alert also covers the IT-worker scheme, which uses AI face-swapping and text-to-speech in video interviews and stolen identity documents to get real jobs. BleepingComputer adds that Japanese authorities have, for the first time, dismantled a North Korean IT-worker operation inside Japan, with evidence of “several hundred million yen” sent abroad. The targets are developers, engineers and IT staff, so the infected device can be a work machine, or a personal one that holds work credentials. Update, 21 September: the Rust project’s security team has warned crates.io maintainers and owners of popular crates that they are being approached by fake recruiters who move to a video call and then ask the target to install a “missing audio codec”; it links the approach to the August hijack of the arrayref crate and attributes the style to North Korea without naming a unit. SentinelLabs’ report on a different North Korean unit, TraderTraitor, using the same lure has its own card below.

_threatfeed.source_name: FBI/IC3 joint alert; The Record; BleepingComputer; Rust security team via SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: Joint alert 18 Sep 2026; Rust security warning 21 Sep 2026

items.title: North Korea’s TraderTraitor put its LayerZero-era macOS backdoors on a DevOps engineer at an Indian IT services firm — the lure was a Terraform lock file in a fake interview project
items.content_text: SentinelLabs reported on 18 September that FLATROOF and ROOFDECK, the Rust macOS backdoors first seen in the LayerZero bridge intrusion, were found on the Mac of a DevOps engineer at a small India-based IT services provider with no cryptocurrency business. The engineer had taken a fake job interview whose take-home project contained a weaponised .terraform.lock.hcl; running terraform init pulled a malicious custom provider. The backdoors, deployed as “SystemUpdate” and “iSync”, run shell commands, harvest AWS and Google Cloud credentials and exfiltrate over Telegram and Nostr relays; ROOFDECK persists through a LaunchAgent masquerading as a Chrome renderer process. Beaconing began on 29 March, with an updated variant on 20 April. SentinelLabs attributes the activity to TraderTraitor, also tracked as UNC4899 and Jade Sleet, a different North Korean unit from the WaterPlum group in the joint advisory above, using the same fake-interview playbook. The victim is not named and downstream customer impact is not discussed. The choice of target is the point: an IT services provider’s DevOps engineer holds cloud credentials for many clients, so one personal decision to run an interview task on a work laptop becomes a supply-chain position.

_threatfeed.source_name: SentinelLabs; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Report 18 Sep 2026; reported 21 Sep 2026

items.title: Fake “LastPass Authenticator” GitHub pages deliver a Microsoft-signed kernel driver that kills 145 security products, then the Rapuncel infostealer
items.content_text: LastPass’s threat-intelligence team and Delphos Labs reported on 17 September a campaign in which search-ranked fraudulent GitHub organisations and GitHub Pages sites, such as one named LastPass-Authenticator, impersonate at least 40 software brands and redirect visitors to attacker servers serving ZIP installers padded to 127–148 MB to get past size-limited scanners. The installer loads a kernel driver, Alinubx.sys, a renamed copy of a driver from a Chinese disk-encryption product that was signed through the Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher chain in March 2023 and is installed as an “NVIDIA File System Filter Driver”. From kernel mode it terminates processes from a list of 145 antivirus and EDR products. The Rapuncel stealer then harvests passwords and cookies from more than 20 browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, Discord, Steam and Telegram sessions, Windows Credential Manager and any file whose name suggests a password, seed phrase or recovery code. LastPass says the signature had not been revoked and the driver was not on Microsoft’s vulnerable-driver blocklist at the time of writing; the lure was first seen in August and was still live in September, and no victim count is known. It is on this page because the driver defeats the one control most enterprises rely on to notice an infostealer, and because the lure is exactly what a well-meaning employee types into a search engine when nobody has told them where the authenticator app comes from.

_threatfeed.source_name: LastPass and Delphos Labs report; BleepingComputer; SecurityWeek; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Report 17 Sep 2026; reported 18–21 Sep 2026

items.title: Ten npm packages hid their payload in library code that runs only when the package is used — built to get past the install-script blocking GitHub introduced in June
items.content_text: Checkmarx has reported indexed-btree, an npm package impersonating the legitimate sorted-btree library, and nine related packages: ordered-kv-index, btree-leaderboard, priority-slot-queue, btree-range-store, btree-core, btree-time-index, btree-lru-cache, neighbor-key-map and sliding-score-window. All ten have been removed from npm. The malicious code does not use preinstall, install or postinstall scripts. It sits inside BTree.prototype.set() and runs when an application actually calls the library, so it slips past the install-script blocking GitHub announced in June 2026. Once running, it collects host details such as hostname, architecture, CPU, memory and uptime and sends them to Slack and Telegram. It fetches commands from a smart contract on the Ethereum Sepolia test network, decrypts a second stage using X25519 key exchange and AES, and can delete files and remove its own triggers. The download figures reported for these packages are likely inflated and have not been independently verified, so they are not repeated here. Checkmarx has not disclosed how many systems ran the code or what the second stage does; its write-up, dated 17 September, does give the Sepolia contract address, 0xE390863Dac96a7118C71227C2b099B50cF602D31, and notes that the source repository was still online after the packages were removed. The lesson is the evasion. Blocking install scripts closes one door, and this campaign used the next one: code that runs inside your application, your tests or your build.

_threatfeed.source_name: Checkmarx; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: Checkmarx research 17 Sep 2026; reported 20 Sep 2026

items.title: An npm package published with valid GitHub Actions provenance carried a loader that runs only when the MCP server starts — Trusted Publishing was abused, not bypassed
items.content_text: CloudSEK reported on 20 September that an attacker with stolen maintainer credentials for the @dforge-core/dforge-mcp npm package changed its CI workflow to publish automatically on push, then shipped malicious versions 0.2.20 and 0.2.21 on 9 September. Because the publish went through the normal GitHub Actions pipeline, the packages carried a valid OIDC provenance attestation; version 0.2.21 was live for about 35 minutes. The payload, which CloudSEK names GHAPPIER, does not run at install time. It executes when the Model Context Protocol server launches, which sidesteps install-script scanning and quarantine in the same way as the runtime-only btree packages on the card above. The loader has been found in 65 public repositories, 73 files and 22 accounts, and its second stage overlaps with the PolinRider campaign that other researchers attribute to North Korea. The scale of downstream victims is unknown. In a related case, Socket reported on 17 September that PolinRider had compromised the GitHub organisation behind the Packagist package visanduma/nova-two-factor and force-pushed malicious code into its development branches, with no tagged stable release found affected. Provenance attestations prove that a package was built by a given workflow from a given commit. They do not prove the workflow was still under the maintainer’s control, and a workflow is one of the things a stolen credential can change.

_threatfeed.source_name: CloudSEK via Infosecurity Magazine; Socket
_threatfeed.date_note: CloudSEK report 20 Sep 2026; Socket report 17 Sep 2026

items.title: The GRIMWEDGE campaign chained two Chrome zero-days and a Windows ALPC bug through a compromised university website — the target was NGOs, the exposure is anyone running unpatched Chrome
items.content_text: Researchers disclosed on 15 September a campaign running since 1 September in which spear-phishing emails sent to non-governmental organisations linked to a compromised US university website, where a reflected cross-site-scripting flaw redirected visitors into a three-zero-day exploit chain. Two of the flaws are in Chrome — CVE-2026-85046 and CVE-2026-87491, the V8 and sandbox-escape bugs Google patched as its seventh in-the-wild zero-day of the year — and the third is CVE-2026-85880, the Windows ALPC elevation-of-privilege flaw that appeared in this month’s Patch Tuesday as an already-exploited zero-day. The chain delivers GRIMWEDGE, a multi-stage JavaScript backdoor capable of reconnaissance, file and process management and command execution, alongside a credential stealer tracked as LONGTALE. Attribution to the China-linked cluster UTA0560, overlapping with JungleBamboo and APT31, is researcher-assessed rather than official. The detail that generalises beyond the victims is the patch gap: fixes existed in the open-source Chromium code before they reached stable Chrome, and the attackers worked inside that interval. A browser is not patched because a fix has been committed, only because the build has shipped and the browser has been restarted. Update, 21 September: Volexity reports that a second China-linked cluster, UTA0565, used the same three-CVE chain through the BlueMoon kit on 3–4 September, while the flaws were still zero-days. It sent Chinese- and English-language phishing to Asian government entities, using lookalike sites impersonating the Center for American Progress (americanprgoress[.]top) and China Digital Times (chinadigitaltimes[.]top). The payload is a new backdoor, CLEANGULP, with shell, file-transfer and BOF-execution features and command-and-control at thecovnresation[.]com. The NGO and media brands were impersonated, not breached. A second group running the same chain fits the shared-kit picture on the Chrome card.

_threatfeed.source_name: The Hacker News; Volexity; Google Chrome release notes; Microsoft security bulletins
_threatfeed.date_note: Campaign from 1 Sep 2026; disclosed 15 Sep 2026; Volexity UTA0565 report 21 Sep 2026

items.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support zero-day CVE-2026-102764 was exploited for about six weeks by a China-linked espionage group before a fix — Mandiant warns of wider attempts
items.content_text: BeyondTrust published advisory BT26-05 on 15 October for CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS v4.0 9.3), improper validation of message origins in Remote Support’s internal messaging components that lets an attacker perform file operations on the appliance. The fix shipped on 8 October and BeyondTrust-hosted SaaS was patched on 9 October; BeyondTrust says it identified the defect on 28 September. Mandiant traced first exploitation to 29 August, against one BeyondTrust-hosted and one self-hosted appliance. The attackers, whom Mandiant and Google’s threat-intelligence team track as Armory Castle (also UNC5221 / Warp Panda) and BeyondTrust describes as state-sponsored espionage, used the Sawfly PHP web shell and the Bareclaw SOCKS5 tunneller, gained root, harvested credentials, deleted logs, moved laterally and took internal documents such as software inventories. Targets include SaaS providers, technology firms, government, legal services and business-process outsourcers, and Mandiant warns of possible widespread exploitation attempts. All Remote Support versions up to 26.2.3 are affected. The flaw is not in the 15 October KEV catalog; its CVE record went public that evening. Remote-support tools hold standing access to the machines they support, which is why a single appliance matters.

_threatfeed.source_name: BeyondTrust advisory BT26-05; Mandiant / Google Threat Intelligence; SecurityWeek; The Record; CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup
_threatfeed.date_note: First exploitation 29 Aug 2026; fix 8 Oct 2026; advisory and research 15 Oct 2026

items.title: A second exploited Cisco Secure Email Gateway flaw, CVE-2026-76519, lets an unauthenticated sender write files and reach root with a crafted attachment
items.content_text: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76519 (CVSS 9.8) on 14 October and says it is aware of attacks this month. A sender with no account can write files to the appliance’s operating system by mailing a crafted attachment, leading to command execution as root, but only when two conditions hold: File Reputation (AMP) is enabled and assigned to a mail policy, and Content Scanner Tools are older than 25.3.0.5525. Cisco found it through internal scanning and has not disclosed how many customers were hit, who is behind it or whether root was obtained; it contacted managed Secure Email Cloud customers with possible compromise. CISA added it to KEV on 14 October with a 17 October deadline. The AsyncOS fix shipped in the same September hardening release that closed CVE-2026-76461 (see that card); Cisco says those are the only two exploited bugs in that release and has not linked them. Secure Email and Web Manager and Secure Web Appliance are not affected.

_threatfeed.source_name: Cisco PSIRT advisory cisco-sa-esa-afw-zqYJkjxp; CISA KEV catalog; The Hacker News; SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: Advisory and KEV listing 14 Oct 2026

items.title: Citrix NetScaler: a fourth critical flaw, CVE-2026-107406, means some appliances patched for September’s exploited zero-days must be upgraded again — CISA has renewed its call to patch
items.content_text: On 8 October Citrix published bulletin CTX697191 for CVE-2026-107406, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider. Citrix rates it CVSS v4.0 9.5 and says it may lead to remote code execution or denial of service; it is not aware of exploitation, and the flaw is not in the 15 October KEV catalog. Builds that fixed the late-September zero-days (14.1-73.37 to 73.41 and 13.1-64.23 to 64.28) remain vulnerable when the appliance acts as a SAML IdP, and older builds are vulnerable as SP or IdP, so those customers must upgrade again. The campaign is still the bigger concern. CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (each CVSS v4 9.5) were exploited before Citrix’s 27 September fix and went into KEV that day, and CVE-2026-88779, a crash bug, followed on 4 October (see that card). CISA has warned that attackers use 88779 to force reboots so that code planted through 88771 runs, and has released Sigma rules. Mandiant counts dozens of affected organisations in North America and Europe and says the actors have suspected state-nexus affiliations, naming no group; Arctic Wolf’s figure of at least 78 counts targeted organisations, not confirmed compromises. Intruders deployed the WHIPSHOT PHP web shell and the SLAPSHOT tunneller. Google’s team traces activity to at least 3 September and Palo Alto Networks to 21 August, and Shadowserver counts more than 20,000 exposed or potentially vulnerable appliances. Patching does not remove access an attacker already has.

_threatfeed.category: Advisory — Exploited zero-days / fourth critical flaw
_threatfeed.source_name: Citrix CTX697191 and CTX697174; CISA KEV catalog and alerts; Google Threat Intelligence / Mandiant; Arctic Wolf; Cybersecurity Dive; The Hacker News; iTnews
_threatfeed.date_note: Exploited zero-days fixed 27 Sep and early Oct 2026; CVE-2026-107406 disclosed 8 Oct 2026; CISA re-patch call reported 12 Oct 2026

items.title: Attackers are chaining two AhsayCBS backup-server flaws for unauthenticated code execution — Ahsay says its August patches did not fully fix them
items.content_text: Huntress reported attackers chaining an improper-authentication flaw, CVE-2026-105133, and a command injection, CVE-2026-105134, in AhsayCBS, the backup server software from Singapore’s Ahsay that many managed service providers run, to plant web shells and XMRig cryptominers. The injection sits in the Replication Receiver API, and the VulDB CNA rates it CVSS v3.1 10.0. Ahsay confirmed that its August 2026 patches, 9.15.2.59 and 10.3.4.0, did not fully close the flaws and has issued hotfixes 10.3.4.45 and 9.15.2.70, which need a reboot; Huntress verified that 10.3.4.45 blocks the initial entry point. CISA added both CVEs to KEV on 14 October with a 17 October deadline. The payload seen so far is a miner, but a backup server holds copies of customer data, which is why a foothold on it matters.

_threatfeed.source_name: Huntress (via The Hacker News); Ahsay; CISA KEV catalog; CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup
_threatfeed.date_note: KEV listing 14 Oct 2026; Huntress findings reported 15 Oct 2026

items.title: SonicWall SMA1000 CVE-2026-102255, a maximum-severity pre-authentication SSRF, drew exploitation attempts two days after its fix — no breach confirmed yet
items.content_text: SonicWall fixed CVE-2026-102255 on 6 October (advisory SNWLID-2026-0017), a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the SMA1000 Appliance WorkPlace interface that lets an unauthenticated attacker make the appliance send requests to internal functionality. CISA’s enrichment data rates it CVSS v3.1 10.0 and SonicWall calls it maximum severity. SMA 6210, 7210 and 8200v on 12.4.3-03526 or older and 12.5.0-02952 or older are affected; the fixes are platform hotfixes 12.4.3-03670 and 12.5.0-03082, and there is no workaround. The same release fixes three authenticated flaws, CVE-2026-102256 to CVE-2026-102258. Defused saw the first hits on its decoys on 8 October and Previdian logged 135 attempts from two US IP addresses. Reporting so far does not establish a successful breach, and the flaw is not in the 15 October KEV catalog. SMA1000 has been exploited repeatedly in 2026; SMA 100 and firewall SSL-VPN are not affected.

_threatfeed.source_name: SonicWall PSIRT SNWLID-2026-0017; CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup; SecurityWeek; The Hacker News; Field Effect; Cybersecurity News
_threatfeed.date_note: Fixed 6 Oct 2026; attempts from 8 Oct 2026; reported 12 Oct 2026

items.title: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 gives an authenticated attacker root through the management interface — exploited as a zero-day and now in KEV
items.content_text: Palo Alto Networks patched CVE-2026-0322 on 14 October, an internally found flaw that lets an authenticated attacker with network access to the management interface run code as root on the firewall, with no special configuration needed. It reports very limited exploitation targeting the management interface and has published three IP addresses tied to the attempts; it names no actor. PA-Series, VM-Series and Panorama (virtual and M-Series) are affected; Prisma Access and Cloud NGFW are not. Palo Alto’s CNA record rates it CVSS v4.0 8.6. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 17 October deadline. Fixed releases cover every supported train, for example 12.2.4, 12.1.10-h2, 11.2.16, 11.1.16-h3 and 10.2.18-h12, with many interim hotfixes listed in the advisory. This is a different flaw from GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257, which ransomware crews are still exploiting (see that card).

_threatfeed.source_name: Palo Alto Networks security advisory; CISA KEV catalog; SecurityWeek; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Advisory and KEV listing 14 Oct 2026

items.title: Microsoft’s October update fixes a record of more than 1,400 CVEs, including CVE-2026-96951, an exploited Windows Shell bypass of Mark of the Web
items.content_text: Microsoft’s 13 October release fixed more than 1,400 vulnerabilities; SecurityWeek counts 1,413 and BleepingComputer 1,411, a record that SecurityWeek attributes largely to AI-driven discovery. One was exploited as a zero-day: CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS 8.8), a Windows Shell security feature bypass that lets a malicious file evade Mark of the Web, so it can run without the usual warning. User interaction is required, and Microsoft has shared no actor or campaign details. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 16 October deadline. It affects supported Windows 10 and 11 releases, Windows Server 2012 R2 to 2025 and Outlook.com, which Microsoft fixed on the service side. Two other flaws were publicly disclosed but are not known to be exploited: CVE-2026-108398, a .NET Framework/WDAC security feature bypass, and CVE-2026-92707, a MessagePack-CSharp denial of service in Visual Studio and .NET. Microsoft has also introduced “risk cohorts” to help customers prioritise, and SecurityWeek separately counts about two dozen Office remote code execution fixes.

_threatfeed.source_name: Microsoft Security Update Guide; CISA KEV catalog; SecurityWeek; BleepingComputer; CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup
_threatfeed.date_note: Released and KEV-listed 13 Oct 2026

items.title: Atlassian’s unauthenticated file-read flaw CVE-2026-21589 is now exploited and in KEV — eight Data Center products are affected, and their configuration files hold credentials
items.content_text: Atlassian disclosed CVE-2026-21589 on 5 October, rated CVSS v4 9.3. An unauthenticated attacker who knows the exact path of a file in a product’s web application root can read it, across Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira, Jira Service Management, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible and Fisheye Data Center and Server. Update: watchTowr confirmed in-the-wild exploitation on 7 October, mostly fingerprinting and sweeps for configuration files, with no post-compromise activity seen at that point, and Previdian logged attempts about two hours after watchTowr published technical details and a public repository. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 15 October with a federal deadline of 18 October. Atlassian Cloud is patched and Bitbucket Cloud is not affected. Fixed versions include Bitbucket 9.4.26, 10.2.8 and 10.5.1; Confluence 9.2.26 and 10.2.19; Jira 9.12.40, 10.3.26 and 11.3.12; Jira Service Management 5.12.40, 10.3.26 and 11.3.12; Bamboo 10.2.24 and 12.1.12; Crowd 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7 and 7.2.4; and Crucible and Fisheye 4.9.15. Atlassian’s interim WAF and rewrite rules are not a substitute for patching. Reading known files is serious on these products, because their configuration files hold database and integration credentials.

_threatfeed.source_name: Atlassian security advisory; CISA KEV catalog; watchTowr and Previdian via The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Disclosed 5 Oct 2026; exploitation confirmed 7 Oct 2026; KEV 15 Oct 2026

items.title: Attackers used an unauthenticated command-injection flaw in Nextcloud’s built-in Collabora server to plant PHP web shells — disabling the app does not fix it
items.content_text: CVE-2026-110447 is a command injection in proxy.php of richdocumentscode, the optional Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app for Nextcloud. Request path content was placed into a bash command, so an unauthenticated request could run commands whenever the local document server was down, for example during a restart, upgrade or crash. The CVE record says it was exploited in September and October 2026, and three Nextcloud administrators reported attacks on GitHub. The first logged attack was on 10 September; attackers dropped one-line PHP web shells named shx*.php under apps/richdocumentscode/, sent uname -a output to webhook.site, and on one server searched for credential stores and crypto wallets. No root access has been reported and the scale is unknown. The fix, 26.4.303, was released on 11 September and needs Nextcloud 30 or later. Standalone Collabora Online and installs that use only the richdocuments connector are not affected. It is not in KEV.

_threatfeed.source_name: CVE record; Nextcloud administrators’ GitHub reports; The Hacker News; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: First attack logged 10 Sep 2026; fix released 11 Sep 2026; reported 14 Oct 2026

items.title: GitLab’s CVSS 10 flaw CVE-2026-97229 could let a crafted CI/CD regular expression run code on the server — self-managed instances need 19.4.2, 19.3.5 or 19.2.8
items.content_text: GitLab fixed CVE-2026-97229 in patch releases 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8. It is an integer overflow in the regular-expression compiler used for CI/CD configuration: a specially crafted regex could let an attacker execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server. GitLab’s CNA record rates it CVSS 3.1 10.0 and describes the attacker as unauthenticated, although the linked HackerOne report is tagged as needing permissions, so treat the authentication requirement as unsettled. GitLab.com is already patched, and GitLab strongly recommends upgrading every self-managed installation immediately. Versions 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2 are affected. No exploitation has been reported and it is not in KEV. A GitLab server holds source code, CI secrets and deployment credentials.

_threatfeed.source_name: GitLab patch release 19.4.2; CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup; Cybersecurity Dive; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: Patch release 12 Oct 2026 (US time); CVE published 13 Oct 2026

items.title: Attackers are probing Langflow’s CVSS 9.9 MCP flaw, which lets any logged-in user run code on the server — weak passwords are the way in
items.content_text: CVE-2026-105740 lets any authenticated Langflow user run code on the server by adding an MCP server that uses the stdio transport: the command field is passed straight to bash -c and runs when the server list is fetched, and the env field allows environment-variable injection. It is rated CVSS 9.9 and affects versions before 1.9.0. Previdian’s honeypots logged 1,423 attempts since 19 September from 27 IP addresses, later 1,706 from 28, with a ramp-up on 11 October; in one sequence the attacker logged in with a common username and password and then used the bearer token on the vulnerable endpoint. Successful compromise has not been confirmed and it is not in KEV. A separate CVSS 9.9 flaw, CVE-2026-105697, is fixed in 1.10.3.

items.title: Next.js ships an out-of-band fix for two critical code-execution flaws, one in the use cache feature and one in SVG handling through sharp
items.content_text: Vercel released Next.js 16.4.1 and 15.5.28 on 14 October. The first critical flaw, GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr (no CVE; CVSS 9.5 from Vercel), is a React Server Components code-execution bug in the use cache feature, affecting 16.0.0 to 16.4.0 apps that use the App Router with Cache Components. The second, CVE-2026-96889 (Vercel 9.5, Red Hat 7.8), allows code execution through librsvg via the sharp image library when an app sets dangerouslyAllowSVG or uses next/og on Node; it needs 16.4.1 or 15.5.28 with sharp 0.35.5 or later. A Server Actions denial-of-service bug (GHSA-p3m5-59mp-jv5r) is fixed too. There is no workaround for the cache and Server Actions flaws. No exploitation had been reported as of 15 October.

_threatfeed.source_name: Vercel / Next.js security advisories; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Released 14 Oct 2026

items.title: Drupal core’s Field UI flaw CVE-2026-108097 can lead to remote code execution through contributed modules — at least one known path needs no login
items.content_text: Drupal fixed CVE-2026-108097 in core on 14 October. Field UI’s table pre-render code executed PHP callables taken from #region_callback without validating them. Core on its own cannot reach the bug, but the Drupal security team says several exploit paths exist through contributed modules and at least one known path needs no login. It rates the issue critical (19 of 25). Fixed releases are 11.4.10, 11.3.19 and 10.6.19; 11.2.x and earlier, 10.5.x and earlier, and Drupal 8 and 9 get no fix. Uninstalling the field_ui module mitigates it. A separate critical remote code execution flaw in the Entity List module, CVE-2026-108099, was fixed at the same time. No exploit code or attacks had been reported as of 15 October.

_threatfeed.source_name: Drupal security advisory (SA-CORE); The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Released 14 Oct 2026

items.title: SAP’s October patch day fixes three critical flaws, in NetWeaver Visual Composer, S/4HANA and Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence
items.content_text: SAP’s 13 October Security Patch Day includes CVE-2026-89110 (CVSS 9.9) in NetWeaver Visual Composer, CVE-2026-89107 (CVSS 9.9) in S/4HANA, which needs only a specific rule-management business role, and CVE-2026-89108 (CVSS 9.1) in SAP Manufacturing Integration and Intelligence (MII), the middleware that links plant-floor systems to the ERP. Also notable are CVE-2026-58249 (CVSS 7.5), an unauthenticated HTTP/2 crash in NetWeaver and Web Dispatcher, and CVE-2026-89113 (CVSS 8.8), SQL injection in Commerce Cloud. No in-the-wild exploitation has been reported. The backdrop matters: the SAPMAP tool released on 15 September bundles proof-of-concept exploits for recently patched SAP flaws, which shortens the time between a fix and its abuse.

_threatfeed.source_name: SAP Security Patch Day; SAPinsider
_threatfeed.date_note: Patch Day 13 Oct 2026; analysis 14 Oct 2026

items.title: F5 fixes critical unauthenticated NGINX buffer overflows and Juniper ships more than 150 Junos fixes — neither vendor reports exploitation
items.content_text: F5 fixed 11 NGINX issues, according to SecurityWeek, including the critical unauthenticated buffer overflows CVE-2026-15176 and CVE-2026-93479, where crafted HTTP requests make the worker restart and could allow code execution if ASLR is disabled or bypassed, plus memory corruption CVE-2026-97205. The Hacker News separately reports open-source NGINX 1.30.6 and 1.31.7 fixing five flaws, among them possible code execution, a TLS bug that may skip client-certificate checks and HTTP/3 request smuggling; the two counts may cover different product scopes. Juniper published 17 advisories covering more than 150 Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved defects plus four in JCNR, about two dozen of them critical, including root code execution, device takeover and kernel panics. Neither vendor mentions exploitation in the wild.

_threatfeed.source_name: F5 K000163408; Juniper security advisories; SecurityWeek; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: NGINX releases reported 15 Oct 2026; F5 and Juniper roundup 16 Oct 2026

items.title: CISA added five long-patched flaws to KEV on 8 October, the oldest from 2015 — BIND, Apache Struts, Strapi, ONLYOFFICE and ProFTPD
items.content_text: On 8 October CISA added five old vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, each with an 11 October federal deadline: CVE-2015-5477, a TKEY denial of service in ISC BIND; CVE-2016-3081, command injection through dynamic method invocation in Apache Struts; CVE-2023-22894, cleartext storage in Strapi; CVE-2021-3199, a path traversal in ONLYOFFICE Docs that may allow code execution; and CVE-2015-3306, the mod_copy file read and write flaw in ProFTPD. CISA lists flaws in KEV when it has evidence of exploitation, but it has not said what prompted these additions, and this page found no reporting on it. Fixes for all five have existed for years, so any system still exposed is probably unmanaged or forgotten.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog
_threatfeed.date_note: KEV listing 8 Oct 2026

items.title: A third exploited NetScaler flaw, CVE-2026-88779, crashes appliances configured for SAML — CISA’s deadline is 7 October, and watchTowr suspects attackers crash boxes on purpose to help the main campaign
items.content_text: Citrix fixed CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway, in bulletin CTX697174. Citrix says it “has observed targeted attacks on unmitigated NetScaler deployments which can lead to Denial of Service”, and that it has not identified an impact on the integrity of customer data. Only appliances configured as a SAML service provider or SAML identity provider are affected. Citrix rates it CVSS v4 8.7. CISA added it to KEV on 4 October with a federal deadline of 7 October; SecurityWeek counts it as the sixth exploited NetScaler flaw CISA has listed in 2026. watchTowr reproduced the bug and describes it as a crash only. It suspects attackers are crashing appliances deliberately to speed up exploitation of CVE-2026-88771, the flaw behind the web shells described on the main NetScaler card (see that card). One researcher reported signs of code execution on patched honeypots; watchTowr and Citrix describe a crash, and this card treats the flaw as denial of service. Appliances patched only to the 27 September builds still need this update.

items.title: Fortinet’s FortiMail has an exploited flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker write files on the appliance — CVE-2026-104286 is in KEV, and Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases
items.content_text: Fortinet published advisory FG-IR-26-175 on 1 October for CVE-2026-104286, a path traversal combined with improper NULL-byte handling in FortiMail that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files on the underlying system through crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests. Fortinet rates it CVSS 9.8 and says it has been reported to be exploited in the wild; one of its own researchers found it. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a three-day federal deadline of 4 October. Affected releases are 7.2.0–7.2.9, 7.4.0–7.4.8, 7.6.0–7.6.6 and 8.0.0–8.0.1. At first the fixed builds were only listed as planned. Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases: upgrade to 7.4.9, 7.6.7 or 8.0.2 or later, and move 7.2 systems to the 7.4 branch or later. Fortinet’s workarounds are to disable identity-based encryption (IBE), restrict webmail and management access to trusted networks, and use WAF rules to block requests containing ../ to the /ibe paths. No actor or victims have been disclosed. A mail gateway sits in the path of every inbound message and is trusted by the mail servers behind it, which is what makes a file-write flaw on it serious.

_threatfeed.source_name: Fortinet PSIRT FG-IR-26-175; CISA KEV catalog; SecurityWeek; Security Affairs
_threatfeed.date_note: Advisory and KEV listing 1 Oct 2026; fixed releases listed 5 Oct 2026

items.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager has an exploited authentication bypass that gives a remote attacker administrator-level access — CVE-2026-76504 has no workaround and is the year’s fifth exploited SD-WAN zero-day by BleepingComputer’s count
items.content_text: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76504 in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager on 30 September and revised the advisory on 2 October. Improper handling of URI encoding lets a crafted request get past an authentication rule meant to restrict access to a specific API endpoint, giving an unauthenticated remote attacker administrator-level access. Cisco rates it CVSS 9.8, says its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in September 2026, and lists no workaround. CISA added it to KEV on 30 September with a federal deadline of 3 October. Fixed releases are 20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1 and 26.2.1; releases older than 20.9 must migrate to a fixed train. No actor has been named. BleepingComputer counts it as the fifth exploited Catalyst SD-WAN zero-day of 2026. SD-WAN Manager is the controller that pushes configuration and policy to the branch routers, so admin access to it reaches the whole WAN.

_threatfeed.source_name: Cisco PSIRT advisory; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: Advisory and KEV listing 30 Sep 2026; advisory revised 2 Oct 2026

items.title: Two Zammad helpdesk zero-days are now in KEV — the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure says they were how an attacker got root on its systems and took volunteer data
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-102489 and CVE-2026-102490 in the open-source Zammad helpdesk to KEV on 2 October with a federal deadline of 5 October. CVE-2026-102489 is a session-fixation flaw that leads to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0–6.5.4. CVE-2026-102490 escalates from that user to root, with a listed range of 1.5.0 through 7.1.0-alpha. The CVE records rate them CVSS v4 8.7 and 8.5, and 9.4 when chained. The volunteer-run Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure (DIVD) found them the hard way. Its case file says the first malicious access was on 21 September, the intruder was detected and blocked on 22 September, and DIVD made its first statement on 24 September. The attacker hijacked a session, ran code, escalated to root, reached other services and took data. DIVD’s 1 October overview says volunteer data got out, such as DIVD email addresses and possibly contact details, and that network segmentation limited deeper access. DIVD believes the attacker was an autonomous AI agent, citing notes the agent left about its own decisions; that is DIVD’s own assessment. It urges anyone running any version of Zammad to update to version 7 or take it offline.

items.title: Apple patched an exploited CoreGraphics flaw that can run code from a crafted file — CVE-2026-86950 is in KEV, with exploitation reported against targeted individuals
items.content_text: Apple fixed CVE-2026-86950, an out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics that can lead to code execution when a device processes a crafted file, in iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1, released on 28 September. CISA added it to KEV on 29 September; CISA’s catalog data gives a federal deadline of 13 October (some mirrors show 2 October, which an earlier edition used). Exploitation has been reported against targeted individuals; no actor or victims have been named. It is rated CVSS 8.8. For most organisations the exposure is concentrated in the people most likely to be singled out, and in devices that are not under management.

_threatfeed.source_name: Apple security release notes; CISA KEV catalog; CIRCL Vulnerability-Lookup
_threatfeed.date_note: Fixed 28 Sep 2026; KEV 29 Sep 2026

items.title: SharePoint CVE-2026-65660 remains under attack with no actor or victim count named — the federal deadline has passed, and a signed-in low-privilege account is all an attacker needs
items.content_text: Microsoft updated its advisory for CVE-2026-65660 on 25 September to say it had reliable evidence of attacks, and CISA added it to KEV the same day with a federal deadline of 28 September, now passed. The code-injection flaw lets an authenticated attacker with low privileges run code on the server with no user interaction, and it is rated CVSS 8.8. The fix shipped in the August 2026 Patch Tuesday updates, but Microsoft first classed the bug as spoofing and only later re-rated it as remote code execution, so teams that triaged August by severity may have deferred it. Reporting lists SharePoint Server 2016, 2019 and Subscription Edition as affected. There has been no new development since: Microsoft has named no attacker or victim count. By 28 September the Previdian platform had logged 16 attempts from two addresses and a web-shell path, /_layouts/15/sphealth.aspx; that is one honeypot’s view, not a measure of a campaign. Symantec’s 1 October Warlock report concerns older SharePoint flaws and does not cite this one (see that card). It led the previous edition and moves here because the NetScaler campaign is broader and better confirmed.

_threatfeed.source_name: Microsoft Security Update Guide; CISA KEV catalog; SecurityWeek; eSecurity Planet (Previdian data)
_threatfeed.date_note: Fixed Aug 2026; Microsoft confirmation and KEV listing 25 Sep 2026

items.title: Mandiant: ShinyHunters is exploiting PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 again by URL-encoding one letter to get past WAF rules — dozens of systems compromised, including at organisations that thought their WAF had it covered
items.content_text: Google’s Mandiant and Threat Intelligence Group reported on 25 September that UNC6240, known as ShinyHunters, has renewed mass exploitation of CVE-2026-35273, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in the Oracle PeopleSoft Environment Management Hub (/PSEMHUB/), rated CVSS 9.8. The flaw was first exploited as a zero-day against education targets between 27 May and 9 June, and Oracle fixed it in June. The new wave requests /%50SEMHUB/ instead, URL-encoding a single letter. WAF rules that match the literal path before decoding miss it, and WebLogic decodes the request and routes it anyway. Mandiant says this reaches “systems whose operators may have believed their WAF rules had mitigated the exposure”. It counts dozens of systems compromised worldwide in higher education, technology and IT services, healthcare, agriculture, transportation and government, names no victims, and says it notified more than 100 organisations whose addresses matched vulnerable endpoints. The intruders dropped JSP web shells (x.jsp, u.jsp, u2.jsp) and Neo-reGeorg tunnels, then a SIDEEYE backdoor hidden in a trojanised, EV-signed Light Alloy installer (Ple64.exe, certificate since revoked) on Windows and MeshCentral agents on Linux, and ran bulk queries against HR, payroll and student records. The same group is behind the FBI jobs-portal breach. ShinyHunters claimed a different PeopleSoft zero-day there, but on 6 October the FBI said the cause was a contractor’s missed patch. Reports link that breach to this CVE; the FBI has not confirmed it, and Mandiant’s report does not mention the FBI. Correction: CVE-2026-35273 has been in CISA’s KEV catalog since 12 June 2026; the previous edition said its KEV status was unconfirmed.

_threatfeed.source_name: Google Threat Intelligence Group / Mandiant; BleepingComputer; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Zero-day wave May–Jun 2026; renewed campaign reported 25 Sep 2026

items.title: Microsoft is tracking attacks on Zimbra mail servers through CVE-2026-73570 — web shells, root access and stolen authentication keys on servers that run the optional SNMP package
items.content_text: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported on 30 September on exploitation of CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra Collaboration before 10.1.20. When the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled, a crafted SMTP request feeds unsanitised input into SNMP notification processing and runs operating-system commands as the zimbra user, with no authentication needed. It is rated CVSS 8.9. The fix shipped in 10.1.20 on 20 July, and CISA added the flaw to KEV on 21 August. Microsoft saw reconnaissance between 28 July and 7 August and exploitation after public disclosure on 13 August. After getting in, attackers dropped JSP web shells, opened reverse shells, escalated to root, installed persistent systemd services, harvested the Zimbra authentication keys zimbraPreAuthKey and zimbraAuthTokenKey, extracted mailbox data and tried to move it out with AzCopy. No actor has been named. Microsoft advises rotating those keys, since patching does not change them.

items.title: Microsoft shipped an out-of-band Exchange Server fix for CVE-2026-96940, which lets a signed-in user read other people’s mailboxes in the same organisation — not exploited, but rated “Exploitation More Likely”
items.content_text: On 2 October Microsoft released an out-of-band security update for CVE-2026-96940 in on-premises Exchange Server. Weak authorisation lets an authenticated attacker elevate privileges over the network and, according to The Hacker News, read other users’ mailboxes, messages and attachments within the same organisation; it does not give access across tenants. It is rated CVSS 8.8. Affected versions are Exchange Server Subscription Edition RTM, Exchange 2019 CU14 and CU15, and Exchange 2016 CU23. Microsoft has applied a related service-side fix to Exchange Online, so cloud customers need do nothing. No exploitation has been reported, but Microsoft rates it “Exploitation More Likely”. The attacker needs only an ordinary mailbox, so one phished account could become access to the leadership or legal team’s mail.

_threatfeed.source_name: Microsoft Security Response Center; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Out-of-band release 2 Oct 2026

items.title: GitLab fixed a CVSS 9.9 sandbox escape in its self-hosted AI Gateway — a user with Duo Agent Platform access could run commands on the gateway server
items.content_text: GitLab released AI Gateway 19.2.4, 19.3.2 and 19.4.1 on 2 October to fix CVE-2026-90970, rated CVSS 9.9. A user with access to the Duo Agent Platform could craft a flow configuration that escapes the prompt-template sandbox and runs commands on a self-hosted AI Gateway. GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated and GitLab-hosted gateways are not affected. No exploitation or public proof of concept has been reported. The attacker has to be a user, but on many instances that means every developer, and any one of them could take over the server that brokers the instance’s AI requests.

_threatfeed.source_name: GitLab patch release notes; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Released 2 Oct 2026

items.title: Kiteworks has lifted its precautionary shutdown advice after deploying a fix, and says it found no sign of exploitation — a separate 1 October batch fixes 126 flaws, including an unauthenticated RCE in its email gateway
items.content_text: Kiteworks, the secure file-sharing and managed file-transfer vendor formerly known as Accellion, asked customers on 25 September to shut their systems down for a weekend window after receiving threat intelligence from federal intelligence authorities. In a 27 September release it said hosted systems had been restored and a fix deployed for a flaw in its Advanced Forms feature, which it says fewer than 1% of customers use. Kiteworks reports no indication the flaw was ever exploited, and it has lifted the shutdown advisory. No CVE has been published for that flaw, and the agency has not been named. Separately, on 1 October Kiteworks published fixes for 126 vulnerabilities, 11 of them critical. The worst, CVE-2026-54154, is an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in Kiteworks Email Protection Gateway before 9.4.1, reported through YesWeHack and not exploited. Kiteworks has not said whether CVE-2026-54154 is the flaw behind the shutdown, so this card does not link them. The card is downgraded from High because the feared attack has not materialised.

_threatfeed.source_name: Kiteworks press releases and advisories; BleepingComputer; The Record
_threatfeed.date_note: Shutdown advisory 25 Sep 2026; restore and fix 27 Sep 2026; advisory batch 1 Oct 2026

items.title: MikroTik RouterOS: CVE-2026-67279 joined KEV on 25 September and, paired with CVE-2026-86060, gives an unauthenticated attacker full control of an exposed router — a separate web-management flaw, CVE-2026-84411, followed in a CISA advisory on 29 September
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-67279 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 September with a federal deadline of 28 September. The KEV entry says the SSH flaw “could allow an unauthenticated client to open a session channel and send an exec request” and “can be chained to achieve unauthenticated exploitation of CVE-2026-86060”, a RouterOS argument-injection flaw. It is rated CVSS 6.9 (version not stated), a score that undersells the chain. CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277 were added to KEV on 10 September. CERT Polska reported on 5 September that a two-flaw SSH chain it calls “MikroTrick” had been exploited in the wild since about 2 September. Its 22 September technical analysis names the chain: CVE-2026-67279 combined with CVE-2026-86060, which gives full administrative control without a password, SSH key or completed authentication. Fixed builds are RouterOS 7.24.2, 7.23.4 and 6.49.21; the related CVE-2026-67278 needs 7.24.3 or 7.23.6 because the earlier fix was incomplete. Shadowserver counted more than 122,500 MikroTik devices with SSH reachable from the internet in early September. That is an exposure count, not a count of unpatched or compromised routers. CVE-2026-67276 is not in KEV. MikroTik routers are common at branch offices, small ISPs and remote sites. Update, 29 September: CISA advisory ICSA-26-272-06 covers a separate flaw, CVE-2026-84411, a pre-authentication integer underflow in the RouterOS web-management interface that can give remote code execution or denial of service. It is rated CVSS v3.1 9.8 / v4 9.3 and fixed in RouterOS 7.24. It is not in KEV, and no exploitation has been reported to CISA.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog; CISA ICS advisory ICSA-26-272-06; CERT Polska (incl. its 22 Sep technical analysis); The Hacker News; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: CERT Polska 5 Sep 2026; KEV additions 10 Sep 2026 and 25 Sep 2026; CISA advisory 29 Sep 2026

items.title: Attackers are probing Rejetto HFS servers for CVE-2026-61500, a flaw found with an AI model that lets them forge an admin session and run code — fixed since July
items.content_text: VulnCheck has reported exploitation activity against CVE-2026-61500 in the Rejetto HTTP File Server (HFS), described as small-scale reconnaissance from a China Telecom address against targets in Japan and the United States. A weak random-number generator used to sign session cookies lets an attacker forge an administrator session and then run code through the server’s scripting feature. It is rated CVSS v4 9.3 (v3.1 9.8). HFS 3.0.0 to 3.2.0 are affected, and 3.2.1, released on 13 July, fixes it. Horizon3.ai found the flaw using an AI model. It is not in CISA’s KEV catalog. HFS is a small file server that people often run ad hoc to share files, so the risk sits in copies nobody in IT knows about.
