items.title: Dell’s Container Storage Modules carry two CVSS 10.0 missing-authentication flaws and four more rated 9.6–9.9 — fixed in 1.18.0, with no workaround
items.content_text: Dell advisory DSA-2026-448, published on 2 October, fixes six critical flaws in Dell Container Storage Modules (CSM), the Kubernetes components that connect clusters to Dell storage. CVE-2026-63688 (CVSS 10.0) is missing authentication on the authorization module’s storage gRPC server, which exposes storage-backend administrator credentials. CVE-2026-63692 (10.0) is missing authentication in the authorization proxy and tenant service. CVE-2026-67269 (9.9) lets a low-privilege user reach root on cluster nodes through the custom-resource reconciler. CVE-2026-54472 (9.8) and CVE-2026-61421 (9.8) are hard-coded credentials and a hard-coded JWT signing key that allow forged administrator tokens, and CVE-2026-67273 (9.6) is a template-engine flaw that allows privilege escalation and RBAC tampering. All versions before 1.18.0 are affected, and Dell lists no workaround. No exploitation has been reported. The prize is storage credentials and root across a cluster, so these matter most where CSM runs in shared or multi-tenant clusters.

_threatfeed.source_name: Dell DSA-2026-448; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Published 2 Oct 2026

items.title: WordPress core CVE-2026-87902 is now in CISA KEV with a 28 September deadline — exploit attempts began within five hours of the fix; update to 7.1.2 even if you installed 7.1.1 earlier this month
items.content_text: WordPress 7.1.2, released on 22 September with backports down to the 4.7 branch, fixes CVE-2026-87902. It is an unauthenticated path traversal that allows local PHP file inclusion and remote code execution, rated CVSS 9.2, and was found by Robert Ressl. Code execution needs two conditions. The active parent or child theme must have a top-level directory whose name starts with page- (such as page-templates), and there must be a readable PHP file outside the theme directories that can be abused. The advisory notes that the official PHP Docker image and the default cPanel configuration with PHP before 8.5 meet the second condition. Patchstack recorded the first malicious requests at 17:44 UTC on 22 September, under five hours after the patch. By 23 September the traffic had increased tenfold and moved from probing with double-encoded traversal strings to writing files such as wp-pear-rce-flag.php, poc87902.php, luci_*.php and zeta_*.php into /tmp and /var/tmp. No confirmed site compromises have been counted. Update, 25 September: CISA added CVE-2026-87902 to the KEV catalog, listing it as remote file inclusion, with a federal deadline of 28 September. This is a different bug from Click2Shell, which was fixed in 7.1.1. Sites updated to 7.1.1 still need 7.1.2.

_threatfeed.source_name: WordPress release notes; Patchstack; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Fixed 22 Sep 2026; exploitation from 22 Sep 2026; escalation reported 23 Sep 2026; KEV 25 Sep 2026

items.title: CISA now says ransomware gangs are exploiting JetBrains TeamCity CVE-2026-63077 — about 160 internet-exposed servers were still unpatched two months after the fix
items.content_text: On 24 September CISA changed its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities entry for CVE-2026-63077 to “Known To Be Used in Ransomware Campaigns”. The flaw is in TeamCity On-Premises, JetBrains’ build server. JetBrains says it lets “an unauthenticated attacker” use the TeamCity agent polling protocol to “bypass authentication checks and execute arbitrary operating system commands.” JetBrains fixed it on 25 July. CISA added it to KEV on 5 August, and JetBrains confirmed in-the-wild exploitation on 7 August. No ransomware group has been named. Shadowserver counted about 160 unpatched TeamCity servers exposed to the internet in late September, down from about 700 after the patch. JetBrains warns that exploitation can “expose TeamCity data, configurations, and stored credentials, modify server state, and potentially compromise the integrity of build artifacts and downstream CI/CD pipelines.” A build server holds signing keys, deployment credentials and source code, so a compromise does not stay on the build server. Any server that was exposed and unpatched after late July needs a compromise check as well as the patch.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog; JetBrains; BleepingComputer; SC Media; Shadowserver
_threatfeed.date_note: Fixed 25 Jul 2026; KEV 5 Aug 2026; ransomware flag 24 Sep 2026

items.title: CISA adds Adobe Commerce/Magento CVE-2026-71362 and WSO2 API Manager CVE-2026-5430 to KEV with a 27 September deadline — one lets attackers into other shoppers’ accounts, the other accepts forged sign-in tokens
items.content_text: Two flaws went into the KEV catalog on 24 September, both with a federal deadline of 27 September. Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source CVE-2026-71362, CVSS 9.1, is an incorrect-authorisation flaw fixed in Adobe’s August bulletin APSB26-92. It needs no login and no user interaction. The Hacker News reports that attackers switch a customer’s session into another customer’s account and read that customer’s private data. Sansec detected and blocked exploitation attempts in August, and Previdian’s sensors saw another attempt on 10 September. Adobe has not yet confirmed exploitation in its own advisory. Affected versions are Adobe Commerce 2.4.4–2.4.9, Commerce B2B 1.3.3–1.5.3 and Magento Open Source 2.4.6–2.4.9 before the August 2026 releases. WSO2 CVE-2026-5430 affects API Manager 4.1.0–4.6.0 and the 4.5.0 and 4.6.0 releases of API Control Plane, Traffic Manager and Universal Gateway. WSO2’s advisory WSO2-2026-5328 says “JWT authentication can be bypassed when a token is signed using an unsupported algorithm, allowing unauthorized access”. It is rated CVSS 10.0 (9.8 in single-tenant deployments) and was fixed in April. watchTowr has seen forged tokens used against it since 13 September. CISA’s own KEV entry titles it a “Multiple Products Path Traversal Vulnerability”. This card uses WSO2’s own description. No attribution has been published for either flaw.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog; Adobe APSB26-92; WSO2 advisory WSO2-2026-5328; The Hacker News; Sansec; watchTowr via SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: KEV additions 24 Sep 2026; deadline 27 Sep 2026

items.title: Roundcube Webmail CVE-2026-48842 is now being exploited, Canada’s Cyber Centre says — a pre-authentication SQL injection fixed in May, with about 523,000 Roundcube instances online
items.content_text: The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security updated its advisory AV26-503 on 21 September to say: “Open-source reporting indicates that CVE-2026-48842 is being exploited in the wild.” It gives no detail on who is exploiting it or how widely. The flaw is an unauthenticated SQL injection in Roundcube’s built-in virtuser_query plugin, where crafted backslash sequences get past the plugin’s escaping. BleepingComputer reports that it can let an attacker bypass authentication, run database commands and steal data from the Roundcube database. SecurityWeek gives it a CVSS score of 8.1. Roundcube fixed it in 1.6.16 and 1.7.1 on 24 May. Shadowserver sees about 523,000 Roundcube instances online, patch state unknown, and exposure depends on whether virtuser_query is enabled. The flaw is not reported as KEV-listed. Roundcube is the webmail front end for many universities, hosting providers, ISPs and smaller organisations, and it often runs on a host’s shared platform that nobody inside the organisation patches.

_threatfeed.source_name: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-503; Roundcube; BleepingComputer; SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: Fixed 24 May 2026; exploitation reported 21 Sep 2026; covered 24–25 Sep 2026

items.title: The Check Point VPN flaw the Dutch NCSC warned about is now exploited — Check Point has seen attacks on Spark firewalls since 12 September, and CISA gave federal agencies until 25 September
items.content_text: This card has changed state. CVE-2026-85102 is improper validation of certificate data during VPN negotiation on Check Point Security Gateways and Spark firewalls. It gives an unauthenticated attacker remote code execution. Check Point released fixes on 9 September (sk1000117). In an advisory on 22 September it said: “Starting September 12, 2026, we observed a wave of exploitation attempts against Spark customers.” Spark is the SMB line, locally or centrally managed, and Help Net Security reports the attempts came from anonymisation infrastructure and were aimed at small businesses and managed service providers. CISA added the flaw to the KEV catalog on 22 September with a federal deadline of 25 September, which has now passed. Check Point gives no customer count and no attribution. It has published usable indicators: exploit certificates with subjects CN=vpn, CN=vpn-user or CN=vpnuser, with OU=users and O=global. The companion flaw from the same NCSC warning, CVE-2026-85103, a heap overflow in the VPN certificate decoder, was not part of the 22 September KEV additions. An earlier edition said there was still a window before exploitation. That window closed on 12 September, ten days before the confirmation. The same Check Point advisory disclosed a second, separate exploited flaw in management servers, CVE-2026-93616.

_threatfeed.source_name: Check Point advisory; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer; Help Net Security; Dutch NCSC
_threatfeed.date_note: Fixes 9 Sep 2026; exploitation from 12 Sep 2026; advisory and KEV listing 22 Sep 2026

items.title: A second Check Point management-server flaw, CVE-2026-93616, was exploited as a zero-day in July — it is not the over-long-username bug, it was fixed on 22 September, and you need to hunt back two months
items.content_text: Check Point’s 22 September advisory disclosed CVE-2026-93616. It is a pre-authentication path traversal in the Security Management web service that lets an attacker execute scripts and load Java classes. Check Point says it saw a “handful of pinpointed attacks on July 23, 2026”, two months before the fix (sk1000171) became available on 22 September. Help Net Security lists the affected products as Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Log Server, Multi-Domain Log Server and SmartEvent. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on 22 September with a federal deadline of 25 September, now passed. Neither the targets nor the actor have been named. This is a different flaw from CVE-2026-91843, the over-long-username stack overflow Check Point disclosed on 16 September, which is not in KEV. Both are on the same servers, so one change window should close both. A management server pushes policy to every gateway beneath it, and this one was exploited for two months before anyone could patch.

_threatfeed.source_name: Check Point advisory; CISA KEV catalog; Help Net Security; The Hacker News; SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: Exploited 23 Jul 2026; fixed, disclosed and KEV-listed 22 Sep 2026

items.title: F5 BIG-IP APM has an exploited unauthenticated RCE, CVE-2026-94127 — only systems where APM acts as an OAuth authorization server are exposed, and the fixes are engineering hotfixes
items.content_text: F5 disclosed CVE-2026-94127 on 22 September (K000162605). It is a heap-based buffer overflow in BIG-IP Access Policy Manager, rated CVSS 9.8 (v3.1) and 9.3 (v4.0), which lets an unauthenticated attacker run code by sending crafted traffic to a virtual server. The condition is narrow. A system is exposed only when an access policy and an OAuth authorization server profile sit on the same virtual server, meaning APM is issuing OAuth tokens. Restricting the management interface does not help, because the attack arrives on the data plane, and Appliance mode systems are equally affected. F5 confirms exploitation but has not described the attacker, the victims or when it started. Rapid7 reported no confirmed public proof-of-concept as of 22 September. CISA added it to KEV on 22 September with a 25 September deadline, now passed. The fixes are engineering hotfixes for 21.1.0, 17.5.0–17.5.1 and 17.1.0–17.1.3, and F5 support can provide a temporary iRule mitigation. The OAuth configuration limits the number of exposed systems. The organisations that run APM this way are usually banks, government bodies and telecoms, where BIG-IP is the front door to single sign-on.

_threatfeed.source_name: F5 advisory K000162605; CISA KEV catalog; Rapid7; The Hacker News; CERT-EU
_threatfeed.date_note: Disclosed and KEV-listed 22 Sep 2026

items.title: Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator has an exploited maximum-severity flaw, CVE-2026-93952 — the SD-WAN controller that pushes configuration to every branch edge
items.content_text: Arista has disclosed CVE-2026-93952, an improper input validation flaw in the certificate-based authentication between VeloCloud Edges and the VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO). BleepingComputer calls it maximum severity, and Arista’s advisory 0183 rates it CVSS 10.0 (v3.1). It is low complexity and needs no privileges or user interaction. The attacker does need network access to the VCO web interface and “the public portion of the VeloCloud Edge authentication certificate”, and certificate-based Edge authentication must be enabled. Arista says the issue “was discovered externally and is known to be actively exploited”. Affected versions are VCO 6.1.3.7 and earlier and 7.0.0.2 and earlier. The fixed releases are 5.2.3.16 and 6.4.2.8 or later. Arista says hosted VCO has been updated, so this is mainly an on-premises problem. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 22 September with a 25 September deadline, now passed. Published indicators include connections from 142.93.149.77 and 104.248.126.159, an x-vc-opt HTTP header, and encoded characters or unusual paths in access logs. An orchestrator compromise matters because the orchestrator configures every edge beneath it: branch offices, shops, clinics and the managed-service customers of carriers.

_threatfeed.source_name: Arista Security Advisory 0183; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer; SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: KEV-listed 22 Sep 2026; Arista advisory and reporting 22–23 Sep 2026

items.title: Cisco ISE has a CVSS 10.0 zero-day under active exploitation — unauthenticated root on the system that decides who gets onto your network, with no workaround
items.content_text: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-76460, a CVSS 10.0 flaw in Identity Services Engine that it describes as insufficient authentication control on an API endpoint. An unauthenticated remote attacker can bypass the web management interface and get root command execution. ISE and ISE-PIC 3.0 through 3.5 are affected. Fixes are in 3.1 Patch 12, 3.2 P11, 3.3 P12, 3.4 P7 and 3.5 P4, and there is no workaround. CISA added the flaw to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 16 September with a three-day federal deadline of 19 September, now passed. The advisory was still at its original revision on 21 September, and Cisco has published no exposure count. No actor has been named, and Cisco warns that attackers may “remove or hide evidence of exploitation”. This is the third actively exploited ISE flaw since June 2025, after CVE-2025-20281 and CVE-2025-20337. It is also Cisco’s second exploited zero-day in a matter of days, after the Secure Email Gateway flaw below. The product’s role is why it ranks among the most urgent items on this page. ISE is the policy engine that decides which users and devices get onto the wired, wireless and VPN network, and what they can reach once there. VulnCheck notes that root on ISE lets an attacker rewrite network access policy, pull stored credentials, delete logs and move laterally. The control meant to contain an intruder ends up working for the intruder.

_threatfeed.source_name: Cisco PSIRT; CISA KEV catalog; CyberScoop; The Hacker News; Help Net Security
_threatfeed.date_note: Advisory and KEV listing 16 Sep 2026; reported 17 Sep 2026

items.title: CISA added a Zyxel GS1900 switch flaw patched in June to KEV on 21 September — GreyNoise ties it to one actor who pulled configs and root hashes from 996 switches in 48 countries, and stole 18,566 government records through WordPress
items.content_text: CISA added CVE-2026-7273 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 21 September with a federal deadline of 24 September. It is a stack-based buffer overflow in the CGI program of Zyxel’s GS1900-series managed switches (GS1900-8, 8HP, 10HP, 16, 24, 24E, 24EP, 24HPv2, 48 and 48HPv2) that lets an unauthenticated attacker on the LAN side execute operating-system commands with a crafted HTTP request; Zyxel published fixed firmware, 2.90(AAHH.2)C0 and per-model equivalents, on 16 June, and its advisory gives no CVSS score. The KEV entry says “LAN-based”, so exposure runs through management-plane reachability rather than the open internet. GreyNoise’s report the same day documents what it calls the first in-the-wild exploitation: a single actor, active since 7 May and assessed as a Chinese speaker, used a PyArmor-obfuscated Python tool to exploit 996 GS1900 switches in 48 countries, led by Italy (133), the United States (129) and Taiwan (123), pulling configurations and root-level hashed credentials over TFTP; 564 of the victims still used factory-default credentials. The same actor exploited two WordPress flaws, CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137, to steal at least 18,566 records, including accounts, plaintext passwords and personal data tied to law-enforcement and government agencies, from an unnamed western government organisation on 22 July, and also worked UniFi OS, FlowiseAI, Gitea (CVE-2026-60004), Nuclio, SENAITE LIMS, Proxmox VE and PAN-OS GlobalProtect. GreyNoise infers LLM-assisted tooling from how the tool iterated; that is an inference. The GS1900 is a small-office switch. It sits in branch offices, schools, shops and labs, is bought without a security review and is rarely on a patch schedule, which is why a June fix is being exploited in September. Update, 22–24 September: BleepingComputer’s coverage of the GreyNoise research adds no new victims. The federal deadline of 24 September has passed, and four more edge and management flaws joined KEV on 22 September (see the Check Point, F5 and Arista cards). No new development was reported as of 27 September.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog; GreyNoise; Zyxel security advisory
_threatfeed.date_note: Zyxel advisory 16 Jun 2026; KEV-listed and GreyNoise report 21 Sep 2026; BleepingComputer 22 Sep 2026

items.title: Cisco’s firewall-management console has three attack clusters on it, including an APT cluster and a ransomware operator — and the hardening advisory, revised on 18 September, is not about exploited flaws
items.content_text: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center remains the clearest example this month of attackers going after the system that manages the perimeter. CVE-2026-20079 (CVSS 10.0) is an unauthenticated authentication bypass that gives root command execution through crafted HTTP requests; CVE-2026-20316 (CVSS 5.3) is a hardcoded low-privilege credential. Cisco Talos separates the activity into three clusters. UAT-12197, unattributed, uses CVE-2026-20079 to plant JSP web shells and a cmd.jar credential extractor. UAT-11823, which Talos tracks as an APT, chains both flaws and deployed a 64-bit Linux variant of the Cyclops Blink malware. Talos notes overlaps with previously documented tooling but does not attribute the cluster to a named group. UAT-11988, which Talos assesses with high confidence to be a ransomware operator, entered through CVE-2026-20316 alone and deployed ransomware on selected endpoints. CISA added CVE-2026-20079 to KEV on 9 September with a 12 September deadline, now passed. Correction: an earlier edition said CVE-2026-20316 had been in KEV since 29 July and was flagged for ransomware use. The KEV catalog has no entry for it; 29 July is when exploitation was first reported. Update, 16 September: Cisco published its September hardening advisory for ASA, FTD and FMC (cisco-sa-hardening-asaftdfmc-uvpPROhN). It covers eight CVEs found in internal review, CVE-2026-20329 to CVE-2026-20336, with fixed FTD and FMC releases 7.0.10, 7.2.12, 7.4.8, 7.6.6, 7.7.13, 10.0.2 and 10.1.0; it went to revision 1.1 on 18 September with an updated ASA fixed-release table. Its statement that two vulnerabilities “belonging to this vulnerability class” are known to be exploited refers to CVE-2026-20079 and CVE-2026-20316, not to the hardening CVEs, which Cisco does not report as exploited.

_threatfeed.source_name: Cisco PSIRT; Cisco Talos; CISA KEV catalog; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: Talos report 9 Sep 2026; hardening advisory 16 Sep 2026, revised 18 Sep 2026

items.title: CISA added three Linux kernel flaws to KEV with a three-day deadline — nobody has said how they are being exploited, which is a reason to move faster, not slower
items.content_text: CISA added three Linux kernel vulnerabilities to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 18 September with a federal deadline of 21 September, which has now passed. CVE-2025-39682 is in the kernel TLS receive path, where a zero-length record gets past record-type handling. The Hacker News gives it CVSS 9.8, and Red Hat cites known public exploits. CVE-2026-53266 is an out-of-bounds write in ebtables SNAT handling that leads to privilege escalation, rated CVSS 8.8. CVE-2025-39964 is a race condition in the AF_ALG crypto socket interface, rated CVSS 7.8. Red Hat has updated its advisories to acknowledge exploitation, but nobody has said who is exploiting the flaws, how, or whether they are being used together. As of 22 September that is still the case. Related but distinct: on 18 September a researcher published working local-root exploits for four other kernel flaws, CVE-2026-80844, CVE-2026-81000, CVE-2026-68121 and CVE-2026-74469, fixed in current stable and long-term kernels, according to The Hacker News. Those are proof-of-concept releases, not KEV entries, and do not overlap with the trio; keep the two sets apart when you brief. CISA’s entries carry two notes worth reading closely: affected products may be end-of-life, and the vulnerable component can be embedded in other products. The second note is where most enterprises are exposed. General-purpose servers get kernel updates through the normal distribution channel, but appliances, network devices, hypervisor hosts and container platforms built on Linux often do not. Local privilege escalation also matters most on shared systems. On a container node, a CI runner or a multi-tenant server, anyone who can run code there counts as a local user.

_threatfeed.source_name: CISA KEV catalog; Red Hat; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: KEV-listed 18 Sep 2026; reported 19 Sep 2026; deadline passed 21 Sep 2026

items.title: A crafted email is enough to get root on a Cisco Secure Email Gateway — CVE-2026-76461 is under active exploitation and there is no workaround
items.content_text: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-76461, a CVSS 9.8 flaw in Cisco AsyncOS for Secure Email Gateway, physical and virtual, that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run arbitrary commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system. Reporting describes the path as SQL injection reached through the appliance’s parsing of an inbound message, which is the uncomfortable part: the attack vector is the product doing its job. No user has to click anything, no management interface has to be exposed, and no credential is needed — the gateway accepts hostile input from the internet by design, and that is the input. All configurations are affected and Cisco states there is no workaround; fixes are in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014, 16.0.4-302 and 16.5.0-780, shipped alongside a security-hardening advisory. Cisco revised the advisory to 1.1 on 17 September to add clarification for clustered appliances; the exploitation statement is unchanged, and the advisory’s own indicator is a search of the mail logs for COPY.*TO PROGRAM. Secure Email and Web Manager and Secure Web Appliance are not affected. Cisco says multiple customers were likely compromised before disclosure and has contacted affected Secure Email Cloud customers with indicators of compromise; attribution is unknown. CISA added the flaw to the KEV catalog on 14 September with a federal deadline of 17 September, now passed. Cisco Identity Services Engine has since followed with an exploited CVSS 10.0 zero-day (see above). Together with Secure Firewall Management Center, SD-WAN Manager and a second exploited gateway flaw disclosed on 14 October, CVE-2026-76519 (see that card), these Cisco products share a shape: perimeter infrastructure that sees everything, trusted implicitly, and rarely covered by endpoint detection.

_threatfeed.source_name: Cisco PSIRT; CISA KEV catalog; SecurityWeek; The Hacker News; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: Advisory and KEV listing 14 Sep 2026; advisory rev 1.1 17 Sep 2026; FCEB deadline passed 17 Sep 2026

items.title: Three JFrog Artifactory flaws chain from anonymous token to administrator in under five minutes — and researchers put half of internet-reachable instances still at risk
items.content_text: Attackers are chaining CVE-2026-42018, a token-disclosure flaw rated CVSS 7.5 that yields an internal anonymous-user JWT even where anonymous access is disabled, with CVE-2026-42016, an insufficient token-validation issue rated CVSS 8.1 that escalates that token to administrator — in some observed cases in under five minutes — before deploying a custom Rust-based command-and-control backdoor. A third flaw, CVE-2026-82329, is a critical authentication bypass in the same product. Attacks were reported publicly from 11 September; Wiz’s timeline puts exploitation of the first two back to 15 August. CISA added those two to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 11 September with a federal deadline of 25 September, now passed, the same day as the four 22 September KEV additions on this page. JFrog has fixed them in 7.111.21 and later, depending on branch. Researchers estimate that between 49% and 62% of internet-reachable Artifactory instances remain vulnerable to at least one of the three. Update, 17 September: Wiz has documented six malicious Groovy user plugins dropped into $JFROG_HOME/var/etc/artifactory/plugins/. They include command shells, a dumper for decrypted LDAP, Crowd and proxy secrets, token tables and signing material, and a memory-resident Tomcat filter backdoor triggered by an X-Request-Trace header. The plugins survive patching and reload on restart, so upgrading closes the way in but leaves the backdoor in place. The severity is not really the CVSS scores, which are moderate individually; it is the position of the product. An artifact registry is the thing your builds trust without checking, so administrator access to it is administrator access to everything compiled, containerised or deployed from it afterwards.

_threatfeed.source_name: JFrog advisory; CISA KEV catalog; Wiz; BleepingComputer; SecurityWeek
_threatfeed.date_note: Attacks reported 11 Sep 2026; KEV-listed 11 Sep 2026; Wiz persistence update 17 Sep 2026

items.title: Google patched the seventh Chrome zero-day of 2026 — and four separate espionage groups were already running the same exploit kit that uses it
items.content_text: Google released a Chrome update on 9 September fixing CVE-2026-87491, an out-of-bounds write in V8, the browser’s JavaScript and WebAssembly engine, and confirmed the flaw is being exploited in the wild. A crafted HTML page is enough to execute code inside the renderer sandbox. The fixed builds are 153.0.8010.36 and .37. This is the seventh actively exploited Chrome zero-day Google has patched in 2026, and it arrives five days after the sixth, CVE-2026-85046, which is also still worth confirming across your fleet. What makes it more than a routine browser patch is who was already using it: researchers found four distinct nation-state-linked groups, one of them APT31 from 28 August, running the same exploit kit — tracked as BlueMoon — chaining CVE-2026-85046 and CVE-2026-87491 inside a single week. Four unrelated actors converging on one chain that fast points at a shared exploit broker rather than four independent discoveries. Two practical notes decide whether you are actually protected. Chrome applies its update on restart, so a fleet where nobody closes the browser is a fleet that is not patched. And every Chromium-based browser in the estate inherits this: Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi and any embedded Electron application ship their own V8 and need their own updates on their own vendor schedules. Update: CISA added CVE-2026-87491 to the KEV catalog on 9 September with a federal deadline of 23 September, now passed. Google has since shipped Chrome 153.0.8010.52 and .53 on 17 September with 16 further fixes, two of them rated Critical (CVE-2026-93374 in the Dawn graphics layer and CVE-2026-93372 in WebGL), with no in-the-wild statement for any of them, so the current build is the target rather than .36.

_threatfeed.source_name: Google Chrome release blog; CISA KEV catalog; The Hacker News
_threatfeed.date_note: Patched and KEV-listed 9 Sep 2026; BlueMoon research 9 Sep 2026; Chrome 153.0.8010.52/.53 on 17 Sep 2026

items.title: The UK government says it will look at using the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill to protect essential services from AI-related risk, and is expanding frontier-AI cyber-defence pilots
items.content_text: On 12 October the UK government, with the AI Security Institute and the NCSC, said it will extend pilots that used frontier AI to find and fix more than 1,000 potential vulnerabilities in government systems, work on how to respond to major incidents involving autonomous AI agents, and examine how serious AI incidents and near misses can be identified and reported. It will also explore strengthening the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill and the wider regime so that essential services such as hospitals and utilities are better protected from AI-related risk, including loss of control. Most of the measures are exploratory and no amendments have been put forward yet. The bill, introduced in November 2025 and carried over into this session, is listed for its House of Lords Report stage on 26 October, a date that may still change.

items.title: The US has reportedly begun staffing a program that would let vetted companies disrupt foreign criminal hacking groups under government contracts — key legal questions remain open
items.content_text: Nextgov reported on 15 October, citing anonymous sources, that the US government has begun selecting managers for a program, unveiled by presidential action in August 2026, under which vetted US companies working under Justice Department or Homeland Security contracts, with written approval for each mission, could gather intelligence on and disrupt systems used by foreign criminal hacking groups. According to the report, payment, liability and legal protections, how targets are chosen, and coordination with the FBI and foreign authorities have not been settled. The government has not published the program’s rules.

_threatfeed.source_name: Nextgov
_threatfeed.date_note: Program unveiled Aug 2026; staffing reported 15 Oct 2026

items.title: The US Senate passed the Health Care Cybersecurity and Resiliency Act by unanimous consent — it now goes to the House, and the HIPAA Security Rule update is reportedly delayed to mid-2027
items.content_text: The Senate passed S. 3315, sponsored by Sen. Bill Cassidy with Sens. Warner, Cornyn and Hassan, by unanimous consent on 1 October after a 22–1 committee vote. As reported by HIPAA Journal, it would require measures such as encryption of electronic health data, multi-factor authentication, ongoing monitoring and penetration testing; designate HHS’s Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response as the health sector’s risk-management agency; require an HHS cyber incident response plan; authorise grants for rural and under-resourced providers; and add fields on recognised security practices to the federal breach portal. It is not law until the House passes it and it is signed. HIPAA Journal separately reports that HHS’s proposed HIPAA Security Rule update has been pushed back to at least July 2027.

_threatfeed.source_name: HIPAA Journal
_threatfeed.date_note: Senate passage 1 Oct 2026; reported 5 Oct 2026

items.title: CIRCIA’s final incident-reporting rule is at White House review and still unpublished — anything quoted as “the rule” today is the 2024 proposal
items.content_text: The final rule under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (CIRCIA) has gone to the White House Office of Management and Budget for review, BankInfoSecurity reported on 2 October. The federal review dashboard at reginfo.gov shows the Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs received it on 1 October and lists it as pending review, and it was still unpublished on 14 October, according to Paubox; HIPAA Journal reports publication is expected before year-end. The federal regulatory agenda had targeted September 2026; the October 2025 statutory deadline and a May 2026 target were also missed. The final text is not public. The figures in circulation, 72 hours to report a covered cyber incident and 24 hours to report a ransom payment, come from the 2024 proposed rule and could change. Infosecurity Magazine quotes an expert who expects the duties to start in late 2026 or 2027. GAO’s 28 September report on overlapping reporting rules (see that card) shows why the final terms matter.

_threatfeed.source_name: BankInfoSecurity; reginfo.gov; Federal Register (Unified Agenda); Infosecurity Magazine; HIPAA Journal; Paubox
_threatfeed.date_note: Received for OIRA review 1 Oct 2026; reported 2 Oct 2026; still unpublished 14 Oct 2026

items.title: GAO’s industry panel says overlapping federal cyber-reporting rules make it hard to report and respond at the same time — DHS and SEC rules are seen as duplicating sector rules
items.content_text: The US Government Accountability Office published GAO-26-109197 on 28 September, drawing on a virtual panel held on 16 July with six industry representatives from energy, financial services and healthcare. Panellists said it could be difficult to fully satisfy all reporting requirements while remediating cyber threats, saw DHS and SEC rules as duplicating sector-specific ones, and half agreed that progress on harmonisation had been limited. They suggested consistent timeframes, thresholds and definitions, a lead agency such as CISA to coordinate reporting, and more collaboration between government and industry. The report makes no formal recommendations. National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross separately pledged on 29 September to harmonise the reporting structure.

_threatfeed.source_name: GAO; Cybersecurity Dive; Industrial Cyber
_threatfeed.date_note: Panel 16 Jul 2026; published 28 Sep 2026

items.title: A Europol-supported operation takes down the KillSec ransomware group’s leak site and arrests three people, including a teenager suspected of leading the group
items.content_text: Europol announced on 30 September an operation against the KillSec ransomware group: three arrests and eight searches in four European countries, the group’s leak site seized and more than 110 TB of stolen data secured. Europol says the suspected leader is a teenager. Outlets give differing counts of the group’s claimed victims, so this card does not state one. The suspects have not been officially named, and this page does not name minors.

_threatfeed.source_name: Europol; SecurityWeek; BleepingComputer
_threatfeed.date_note: Announced 30 Sep 2026
